extracted.intended_audience: beginner and developing stand-up comedians and comedy coaches
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing, structuring, performing, and assessing a five-minute stand-up comedy set, plus supporting workflows (premise-first writing), memorization, mic technique, and recording/review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opener (60s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opener (60s): establishes who you are, why we should listen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First ~60 seconds should introduce persona and give the audience a reason to pay attention; sets the tone for the set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bit 1 (60s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bit 1 (60s): short, punch-dense bit; demonstrates competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, high-density joke early to show skill and land laughs quickly; demonstrates the comedian can deliver tight material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bit 2 (90s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bit 2 (90s): longer story; demonstrates range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A longer narrative or story to show storytelling ability and emotional or comedic range; allows development beyond quick punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bit 3 (60s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bit 3 (60s): punchy, returns to opener's energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shorter, energetic bit that brings energy back toward the close and connects tonally with earlier material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closer (30s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closer (30s): callback or strong button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final ~30 seconds should be a callback or a strong comedic button to leave the audience satisfied; tight ending is crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-minute set as assessment unit / shape matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The five-minute set is the unit of stand-up assessment. The shape matters as much as the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should judge both the structural flow (opener → bits → closer) and the quality of individual jokes; consider pacing and energy arc as central to assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write 50 premises
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 50 premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-volume ideation step to generate raw material; quantity first to find strong, belief-driven premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick the 5 you most believe
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick the 5 you most believe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select premises that feel authentic and that you have conviction about — belief in the premise improves performance and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate 5 jokes per premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate 5 jokes per premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create multiple angles and punchlines for each chosen premise to explore its comedic potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick the strongest joke per premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick the strongest joke per premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the best-performing or most convincing joke for each premise to build into material; be ruthless about discarding weaker bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set/order them by energy and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Set order them by energy and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence jokes to create an energy arc and tonal coherence across the set rather than placing jokes arbitrarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage-test for 10 sets before re-evaluating
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage-test for 10 sets before re-evaluating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform material multiple times (recommended ~10 sets) to gather reliable feedback and detect which jokes consistently land before major rewrites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorize the BEATS, not the words
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorize the BEATS, not the words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn the structural beats and timing rather than word-for-word lines so you can stay reactive and natural onstage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid word-perfect memorization (sounds canned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word-perfect memorization makes you sound canned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly memorized scripts can sound robotic; prefer flexible recall to allow for audience interaction and organic timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat memorization allows room to react
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat memorization gives you room to react to the room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing beats enables improvisation and adjustments based on audience responses while preserving the set structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouth 3–6 inches from mic
rubrics_metrics.description: Mouth 3–6 inches from mic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent distance for clear audio and controlled vocal dynamics; practical microphone placement guidance for live performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't hide behind the stand
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't hide behind the stand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stage and visibility; avoid physical barriers between you and the audience to increase presence and connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye contact with three sections of the room
rubrics_metrics.description: Eye contact with three sections of the room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spread attention across the space to engage the audience broadly rather than focusing narrowly; divides room roughly into three sightlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: The mic is an instrument; learn it
rubrics_metrics.description: The mic is an instrument; learn it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat microphone technique as a performance skill—use proximity, tilt, and movement intentionally to shape delivery and comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record at minimum audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio at minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always record sets; minimally capture audio so you can review pacing, wording, and laugh timing even if video isn't available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen at 1.5x speed for pacing diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen at 1.5x speed for pacing diagnostic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster playback helps identify pacing issues and dead spots quickly when reviewing recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen at 1x speed for word choice diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen at 1x speed for word choice diagnostic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal-speed listening helps evaluate phrasing, wording, and naturalness of delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate every laugh, miss, and silence
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate every laugh, miss, and silence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed annotation of recordings provides data for where jokes land, timing issues, and where rewrites are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working rubric: clear set shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the five-minute set have a clear shape (opener, bits, closer)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the set anatomy as a structural checklist when assessing whether the set feels complete and cohesive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working rubric: sequencing for energy flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Are bits sequenced for energy flow, not arbitrary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ordering for an energy arc; poor sequencing can undercut laughs even if individual jokes are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working rubric: memorizing beats, not words
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you memorizing beats, not words?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that performer is flexible and responsive rather than reciting word-perfect lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working rubric: commanding the mic and room
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you commanding the mic and the room?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess stage presence, mic technique, eye contact, and whether the performer occupies the space confidently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working rubric: recording and reviewing every set
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you recording and reviewing every set?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular review practice is required for iterative improvement; absence of recordings hinders reliable evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working rubric: tracking jokes across 10+ sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you tracking which jokes have hit in 10+ sets?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-set tracking to determine consistent hitters vs. flukes; require ~10 performances to judge a joke's reliability.
